newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma wheat condition declines slightly in week.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma wheat condition declines slightly in week.

text.p: Oklahoma's wheat condition declined slightly in the week ended Sunday as dry weather prevailed, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday in its weekly crop weather report.

"Dry conditions across western and central parts of the state have caused wheat condition to decline slightly. Warm weather during the week has kept wheat development progressing ahead of average," the report said.
Wheat condition was rated nine percent excellent, 70 good, 19 fair and two poor. That compared to last week's rating of 13 percent excellent, 70 good, 15 fair and two percent poor.
Wheat acreage jointing was reported at 61 percent, versus 16 last year and 42 percent for the five-year average.
Greenbug, aphid and armyworm infestations were on the rise, and growers applied control measures in many areas. Soil-borne mosaic virus and rust were reported in some fields.

Topsoil moisture condition was rated 11 percent surplus, 64 adequate, 21 short and four very short. That marked a decline from last week's ratings of 13 percent surplus, 72 adequate, 12 short and three very short.
Pasture and range condition increased slightly, as cool season grasses greened up rapidly with the warmer weather.
